$comment: The single source for every constant the interfaces share.
This file exists for one reason: MultiTask Manager ships a macOS client and a
Windows client from one engine, and two hand-maintained constant files drift.
They do not drift dramatically — they drift by two points of padding and one
shade of orange, which nobody notices until the two apps sit side by side.
Sources/MultiTaskCore/Design/DesignTokens.swift is GENERATED from this file by
Scripts/generate-tokens.py, and a test fails if the two disagree. Edit this
file, run the script, commit both.
Colour is the exception, and deliberately so. See notes in `color`.

spacing.$comment: A 4pt base with 2 and 6 as half steps, because a dense menu bar list genuinely needs the half steps and inventing them per-view is how 1, 3, and 5 got in.
spacing.$comment2: `spacious` is for empty states only — the one place in the app with room to breathe, because an empty state is the only screen nobody is scanning.

radius.$comment: Two only. A third radius is a decision nobody remembers making.

size.$comment: Popover width is the one hard number in the design: 380 fits a project row with a status glyph, a title, and a menu affordance without truncating at the default system font, and stays narrow enough not to look like a window.
size.$comment2: Two dot sizes, named by role rather than by number. A run's state sits on its own line and takes the larger dot; a marker beside caption text takes the smaller. Two role-named sizes are a decision; two bare numbers are drift.
size.$comment3: Indent for content nested under a row, derived so it stays aligned with the glyph above it if the glyph changes: statusGlyph + row + tight.

$comment: Semantic system fonts, not point sizes, for everything a person reads.
That is not laziness: on macOS the semantic fonts follow the user's text-size
and accessibility settings, and a menu bar utility that ignores those is
unusable for the people who change them. The explicit sizes below are only
for things that are not prose — a monospaced command line, a glyph.
Windows maps the roles to its own type ramp.

mono.$comment: The confirmation sheet and the run command. Monospaced because misreading a path or a flag is the failure this text exists to prevent.

$comment: Semantic ROLES, mapped by each platform to its own system colour — not hex
values baked into two apps.
Green means *finished*, never *in progress*, and never *all clear*. It carried
all three at once, which made it mean nothing: a working agent, a healthy
detector, and an empty queue were the same colour. Calm is now the absence of
colour — nothing coloured in view is itself the signal that nothing needs you.
This is a deliberate rejection of a custom status palette. System colours
already satisfy contrast in light and dark, already respond to Increase
Contrast and to the colour-blind accommodations in macOS, and already look
native next to every other menu bar item. A hand-picked orange would have to
re-earn all of that, and would fail quietly for exactly the users who need it.
`fallback` is for platforms with no system equivalent, and for documentation.
It is never the preferred source on macOS.

attention.meaning: Something is waiting on the person. The only role permitted to interrupt.

working.meaning: Progressing on its own. No action wanted. Shares the accent with `ready` on purpose: neither asks anything of you, and the glyph separates them.

complete.meaning: Finished. Worth seeing, not waiting on you. Green belongs here — it reads as *done* everywhere else in software, which is why using it for work in progress was a mistake.

idle.meaning: Stopped with nothing queued. Noticed, never interrupting — orange stays the only role permitted to interrupt, so this reads as waste rather than as a question. Distinct from `dormant`, which is the same absence after a week and is genuinely not urgent.

blocked.meaning: Waiting on something impersonal — a dependency, another task.

dormant.meaning: Quiet with nothing ready. Reported, never highlighted.

unknown.meaning: The app cannot tell. Distinct from 'nothing is happening'.

emphasis.$comment: Opacities for the one grouped, bordered block the design allows — the asks section. Kept here so a second such block cannot invent its own.

$comment: There is almost none, on purpose. This is a status surface read in a glance
while thinking about something else, and animation on a list that refreshes
every few seconds turns a glance into a wait.
Nothing animates on a data refresh — a row that slides when a number changes
makes the list feel unreliable. Only direct manipulation animates.
Both durations must be skipped entirely under reduced-motion.
